messages:
zoe parker: hi folks, quick org question as I'm digging through onboarding: who owns approvals for data-access requests (esp. customer data), who signs off on Dedicated capacity spend, and who is the reviewer for model rollout approvals? trying to map out who to cc in tickets.
Lena Ortiz: welcome Zoe! short answers: Security owns PII/data-access reviews, Finance owns billing/commits for Dedicated, and Platform/Product own rollout approvals (depending on model).
zoe parker: thanks! can you name people or channels? want to avoid pinging the wrong group.
Lena Ortiz: Security: use `#eng-security` and tag @Lena Ortiz for anything that needs an exception. For formal access reviews open a ticket with the security queue (tag `security-access`).
Mike R.: Dedicated capacity approvals: start a request in the finance portal, tag `redwood-dedicated` and CC `#finance`. For anything > $50k/yr loop in @VP Finance — finance-bot will flag it.
finance-bot: Note: requests >$50k/yr require CFO approval and a cost forecast attachment. Use template `dedicated-request-v1`.
zoe parker: great. model rollout approvals — is there a checklist or owner list?
Alex (Platform): Platform owns runtime compatibility and safety checks; Product owns quality/regression signoff. For model rollouts please follow the rollout playbook in Confluence: `Platform/rollouts/model-rollout-playbook`. Key reviewers: Platform on infra risk, Product PM on quality, Security for data concerns.
zoe parker: is there an SLA for review turnaround? trying to plan my timeline.
Lena Ortiz: typical security review is 48-72 business hours for routine read-only grants. If it's urgent, add `priority: high` and include an exec sponsor.
Mike R.: Finance approval depends on commitment size; small spikes or trial capacity can be approved in ~3 business days if you include justification and expected utilization.
zoe parker: who signs off on monitoring and alerting post-rollout? want to make sure ops coverage is set.
Alex (Platform): Ops/Observability is `#eng-sre` — have them sign the runbook before rollout. Also add a tracing/alerting checklist to the rollout ticket: pages, thresholds, runbook link.
zoe parker: useful. for customer data access, do we ever use short-lived credentials or proxies? trying to propose a safer path.
Lena Ortiz: yes, we prefer short-lived creds or via a read-only service account that has an approval expiry. Security enforces just-in-time where possible.
zoe parker: perfect. any escalation matrix if reviews are blocked and a release is time-sensitive?
Alex (Platform): escalation: 1) escalate in-ticket to team leads, 2) ping channel (e.g., `#eng-security` or `#finance`) with `urgent` tag, 3) if still blocked during release window, call the release lead and post in `#release-war-room`. We keep a pager for release-day emergencies.
zoe parker: can someone point me to the template for requests and rollout checklist?
Mike R.: attaching quick templates below (copy into request):

```
DEDICATED REQUEST TEMPLATE
- Team: <team name>
- Purpose: short justification + expected qps
- Requested capacity: GPUs/nodes or dollar amount
- Duration: trial / 3mo / annual commit
- Owner to notify on cost overruns: <person>
```

```
MODEL ROLLOUT CHECKLIST
- Model version and hash
- Eval suite pass rates + regressions
- Monitoring + alert thresholds
- Rollout plan (canary %, timeline)
- Rollback steps and owner
```

Lena Ortiz: i'll drop links to the official templates in `#new-hires` pinned message.
SecurityBot: Security checklist reminder: include dataflow diagram if customer data will be accessed; add DLP tag if necessary.
zoe parker: thank you all — this clarifies a lot. i'll open the relevant tickets and link back here.
Alex (Platform): welcome aboard and ping me if you need a quick runthrough of the playbook.
zoe parker: appreciate it! closing thread once tickets are created. :sparkles:
thread_text_snippet: who owns approvals for data-access, Dedicated spend, and model rollout approvals
